findings.reason: The protected source is the conventional optimal parent-pointer solution: it isolates the right-subtree minimum case, then climbs only through completed right-child chains. The short control flow, identity comparisons, and `successor` and `current` names expose the inorder reasoning directly, so no inert candidate is materially justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 510 and its Python Node-to-optional-Node contract. The app source defines the required local equivalent of LeetCode's injected parent-pointer `Node`, returns object identity rather than a value, needs no separately supplied root, and uses no value lookup, satisfying the source follow-up.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2065163839. It and the protected app source have identical right-child detection, leftmost descent, `current` initialization, parent climb condition based on object identity, and final optional-parent return. Differences are limited to the app's local Node definition and the native class/type wrapper.

The balanced-tree workloads contain 31, 127, and 511 nodes, span more than 16x, and query the maximum so the reviewed source climbs only the tree height while a whole-tree method must traverse all nodes. The protected source passed all 10 correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 10,000-node boundary. A correct full-inorder control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict with relative growth exponent +0.75 and a 21.53x largest runtime ratio.

The current-targeted Approach exactly explains the mutually exclusive leftmost-right-subtree descent and parent climb, why right-child ancestors are already visited, why passing the root means no successor, and how identity-only navigation satisfies the no-values follow-up. Its O(h) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the source.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the authenticated Premium statement. It preserves the successor definition, direct-node and parent-pointer model, Node fields, object return semantics, both explained examples, all three constraints, and the no-value follow-up in source order. Both source tree images were independently recreated as accessible Mermaid diagrams with the same nodes and parent-child relationships.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact level-order trees, selected nodes, and successor values. The invented third sample was correctly relabelled as a trial.
Both formerly hidden correctness cases are now visible trials, and every fixture selects an existing node from a valid binary search tree with unique values and correctly wired parent links.
Boundaries cover one and 10,000 nodes, values -100000 and 100000, roots, internal nodes, leaves, the minimum node, the maximum node, and both a successor and a null result.

Material semantics cover a direct parent successor, climbing through multiple completed right-child ancestors, a direct right-subtree minimum, a deeper left descent inside the right subtree, a single-node tree, and returning the exact Node object rather than merely its value.

An independent inorder identity oracle verified all ten correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected implementation returned the exact expected object across 5,039 exhaustive small-BST queries and 1,000 randomized BST queries.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 31-, 127-, and 511-node balanced-maximum workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
